name: Til Gahori
ingredients: 500g pork (belly or shoulder, cut into medium cubes)
4 tbsp black sesame seeds (dry roasted and ground into a paste)
instructions: 1. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or pressure cooker until it reaches smoking point and then cools slightly.
2. Add the chopped onions, crushed ginger, and garlic; sauté until golden brown.
3. Add the pork cubes, turmeric powder, and salt. Sauté on high heat until the pork is lightly browned and releases its fat.
4. Add the slit green chilies and the black sesame paste, mixing thoroughly to coat the meat.
5. Add water, cover, and cook on low heat (or pressure cook for 3-4 whistles) until the pork is soft and the gravy thickens to a semi-dry consistency.
6. Serve hot with steamed rice or Jolpan.
description: Til Gahori is a signature delicacy of the Ahom community in Assam. The combination of succulent pork and the earthy, nutty flavor of black sesame seeds (Til) creates a unique flavor profile that is quintessentially Assamese, often prepared during celebrations like Magh Bihu.
